wac.note: WAC TWI = fraction of time-weighted WAC observations in which the 100 m pixel was lit, one lunar year (15 Feb 2010 - 5 Feb 2011, 3807 images). Ours: same period, 2 h, 0.5 m above ground, any part of the Sun disc visible, mean of 5 points within 25 m. PGDA 69: 18.6-yr modelled average, 60 m. Registration check over all of 88–90° S (950,380 pixels): WAC vs PGDA 69 Pearson r = 0.956, and every flipped orientation is near 0, so the map is placed correctly. Up to 50 % the two agree bin by bin within ~2 pts (PGDA 69 40–50 % → WAC 39.1 %), but WAC compresses bright spots: PGDA 69 70–80 % → WAC 52.2 % (WAC maximum 71.7 %). So WAC validates the regional pattern but cannot rank well-lit landing sites; at these 17 RoIs every model reads ~30 pts above it.

barker.note: 5 m above the surface, 1 Jan 2024 – 1 Jan 2026 hourly, visible Sun-disc fraction averaged over 5 sampled pixels per RoI. Our worst-of-20-clones minus Barker's 1st percentile of 100: mean +0.06, range -0.38 to +0.66 pts; nominal minus Barker: mean +0.74 pts; rank correlation 1.00. RoI 4 (Barker's 88.1 %): nominal 88.2 %, worst clone 87.7 %. Differences: 5 pixels not the full RoI, 20 not 100 clones, our 720-bin horizon vs Barker's method. On the NASA GSFC SfS terrain instead of LOLA: mean +0.86 pts vs Barker (range -0.29 to +2.35).
